[quote=lyuongo_national_salvation_army;61613553]Uria had fallen indeed, but the Aokashima attacks on the LNSA had royally broken the back of their communications, and it would severely damage the LNSA's fighting capability, as many fell to the drone attacks and bombing runs of the Air Force. The National Salvation Navy was completely sunk, or generally rendered useless, though the Honoured Marshal didn't particularly care for their deaths. The National Salvation Army would be halted for several days as they attempted to beat the cyberattacks, though the general digital incompetence meant they gave up, it wasted several days before Hein decided to simply begin transmitting messages via motorcycle. Several hundred would die to the half-assed bombing Republican runs - perhaps due to a miracle. 

Hein would ultimately decide to dispatch riders to the northern jungle Inferno Divisions and order them back to Yapinaw, along with around a quarter of the National Salvation Army, the rest would be mounted in Furinau. Hein would order an assault towards Durgo, with a large convoy going straight on the national highway, and several squads going through the rainforests. If any neared Durgo without being spotted, they would set fires, and if they encountered any Tigerian villages, they would likewise be burnt and eaten. Once again, Hein was uninformed due to the Aokashima disruption of communication. Hein would remain in Yapinau, though in a cellar, largely to avoid more bombing runs. He would plot out the coming war using a child's confiscated toy soldiers and a pack of smokes.

Hein would order whatever aircraft not bombed out to follow the convoy going to Yapinau, to bomb Durgo and any positions spotted from the sky, though it would largely be ineffective with the lack of communication, still, a bombed city is a bombed city!

[i]"The loss of the navy is annoying, however, the admiral was largely going insane. It is perhaps better for our revolution that he is dead."[/i]
[b]~ Honoured Marshal Hein on the death of the Admiral[/b][/quote]
[pre]FRIDAY, 9th OF JUNE, 2028[/pre]
[i]Over the dark, damp jungle on the approach to Durgo, pillars of fire bloomed like vibrant flowers in the dead of night. LNSA forces had made their move towards the LNA-occupied city of Durgo in response to the ealier bombing raid of the city by the Lyuongo Air Force. Rushing to their humvees, the men of the Durgo branch of the Lyuongo Rapid Support Forces grabbed their black rifles and their sleeveless-camoflauge jackets before heading out to the National Highway. Small LNA contingents were already spread among the jungle heading up to Durgo, and they would be the first ones to meet LNSA forces in close quarters combat in charred nonite villages. Human soldiers used nonite corpses as all sorts of things... for cover, to set up traps for incoming enemy vehicles, their hides as jackets once the rain came in late into the night... As for the Highway, the scrambled rapid response forces skidded their humvees across the wet pavement, setting up a front using their armored vehicles. Behinf the humvees, the men of the RSF set up positions with their rifles and on the roof of the humvees, their .50 cal machine guns. Stalemate washed over the fighting, with the deep mud in the jungle making any advances pass the burnt villages all but impossible, and the no-mans-land of scattered bullets over the highway turned anyone daring enough to advance into hamburger. Both Air forces occupied each other over the air in Durgo, with the republican air force vehemetly defending the area around the Durgo Air Base.[/i]

[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61637347][b]August 4, 2028: Hell on Erene[/b]

[b]The Sallacher Invasion[/b]

Henri sat at the table with his advisers and Eleonore, video footage of Knygta and Deyn playing across the wide screen televisions that lined the walls of the situation room.

Knygta and Deyn just seceded yesterday, and nowwe have a former medieval duchy or principality, invading a former duchy, stated Henri slowly trying to process the events of that morning.

Yes sir, replied General De Funes.

Henri sighed, Do we have a ground situation on Belgarde? 

Sallach forces entered the duchy last night, numbering approximately 6,000 with a tank division, replied De Funes, They managed to secure two airfields approximately 20 and 30 kilometers from the border, 

What about resistance? Asked Henri.

Given the speed at which they traversed 20 to 30 kilometers, Id say none, replied De Funes.

Any word from the regime? 

The regime, your majesty, has been slow to react, we suspect a lack of resources or thinly stretched resources, as well as cooperation on the level of the government of Belgarde, replied Jalouse.

Henri nodded, While this wasnt in our plan book, well roll with it, General De Funes, prepare a back up contingency of 7,000 Gendarmerie and two tank divisions,

The general nodded and stood up to make some phone calls.

[b]The biggest crashout[/b]

WHERE ARE THE SOLDIERS! Screamed Haakon Strømm as word of the Sallach incursion reached him.

They havent been able to centralise yet, replied Begren, The situation is changing too fast,

Dont we have bombers?! Demanded Haakon.

We can deploy them, replied Begren.

Then bomb these troops to sh-t commander!

Begren nodded and left the room to order any airforce pilots or commanders still loyal to the regime to scramble their jets.

As Begren walked out of the office and down the hall, an officer approached him, stopping and saluting him. He spoke, Sir, we have received reports that the administration in Belgarde intends to surrender to Sallach, they complain that there is little aide from the central command and that there is little ability to coordinate. 

Bergen scoffed as he began walking down the hall once more, motioning for the officer to follow him.

Are you aware of the rules of combat sir? Asked Begren.

A little, I was taught them at the academie, replied the officer.

Then you are familiar with the laws and regulations regarding combatants, continued Begren.

Yes, replied the officer.

What do you think secessionists count as? Pressed Begren.

Enemies of the state? Asked the officer unsure.

Bingo, ergo, they are lawful combatants, replied Begren, Especially if they have formed militias,
Sir I do not understand, how does this relate to the situation at hand? asked the officer.

Well, youll see, you will see, replied Begren with a grim smile.

[b]The Command[/b]

Lieutenant Wjlliam House could feel the power of the F-35 rumbling along the strip of the tarmac at Haakon E. Roelffe Airbase, located in Mittlemarkke approximately 50 km from the capital in the north.

The situation on the ground was chaotic, apparently Mittlemarkke was one of the few regions where commands and orders were actually reaching soldiers, primarily due to the internet and comms shutdown affecting the channels the armed forces usually used during situations like these.

However, his superiors had assured him and his airmen that there would be full restoration of connectivity within the next twenty four hours, as the SCSID had begun to activate its special command channels.

House pushed on the throttle as the control tower chattered into his earpiece, he leaned slightly back in the seat, and the plane throttled forward down the runway reaching a breakneck speed as it lifted off.

Upon reaching the desired altitude, House turned towards Belgarde, asking for a clarification on the coordinates of the forces he was required to strike, they were repeated to him twice. 

As he breached the border of Belgarde, the comms sprung to life once again, this time a different voice spoke, There has been an attempted attack by the Sallach forces, they have breached the city of Wavre, and are attacking the royal palace, evacuations in place, 

House shrugged off the information, unsure whether the comm had been meant for someone else or was merely an update, he turned northwards, towards the region where he had been told the forces were expected to be found, beginning a short descent to get within firing range.

The comms crackled on Wavre-23, turn to Wavre, 

House frowned, he knew Wavre, it was a dense medieval city, there was no way that they expected him to bomb any location within the city, unless the ground forces had managed to evacuate citizens.

Wavre-23, turn to Wavre repeated the order.

Can I get a clarification on that order? asked House.

Wavre-23, repeated the voice, Turn to Wavre, CENTCOM, fire at the given target, Sallach forces in city, 

House turned the plane, noting out of his cockpit another plane, the same model as his had joined him, the pilot gave him a thumbs up, Were turning to Wavre, said the voice of the pilot over his headset.

Yea, I know, I dont know why, replied House as the fighter planes continued onwards

They descended lower as the outskirts of Wavre came into view, Its the city square ya? asked House.

Yes, replied the other pilot, I am readying my missiles, 

House frowned, On the count of 3 right? he asked.

Yes, replied the other pilot, the centre of the city appeared, the cathedral of Wavre standing tall over the main square, a massive crowd had formed in the square.

1 began the other pilot, Houses finger hovered over the release trigger, those werent soldiers, 2 continued the other pilot, Bombs away! declared the other pilot as House immediately jerked the plane away from teh city centre, hearing the massive explosions as they hit the square from a distance, the other plane continuing on a straight course before banking back towards the base it had come from.

[b]Belgarde[/b]

Antoine Jacques strolled through the halls of the ducal palace, he had been placed as the temporary regional administrator of Belgarde following the arrest of the duc, and had spent very few days in office.

The morning of August 2nd had come as a shock to him as Knygta and Deyn declared effective independence from Rosenmarkke. His mind had lept to the secessionist movement in Belgarde and their reaction, predicting to the general of the Central Belgarde Forces (which had been ordered under the centralisation order days earlier) that protests would most certainly sweep the region in the following days.

However, he had not expected a full northern invasion by the principality of Sallach, as such, he had risen from the office of the duc and begun to wander the halls, his cane tapping the carpet, head bent in thought.

The regime was unstable and rapidly collapsing, only the loyalty of the remaining ducs and the armed forces mattered in any form of preservation, and these acted only as temporary forces of preservation.

If perhaps he surrendered to the Sallach forces they would provide an amnesty agreement for his involvement in the regime, however, where Sallach moved, Montfleur was bound to follow.

Then there were the protests, he stopped to listen to the growing roar in the palace square, the protests were closer than the Sallach army, and he had ordered the guards to show maximum restraint.

The sound of jets roared over the palace, the palace suddenly shook violently as windows suddenly burst indward, the roar of the crowd suddenly turned into chaotic screams

Antoine found himself knocked over against a table shielding his face from the bits of glass that showered the hall as he espied thick smoke from the square.

Staggering to the broken window he espied half the square covered in gore and soot, half of a building blown to bits as the surviving protestors fled with some attempting to drag the wounded out of the carnage.

The bastard government had bombed their own citizens, Antoine clutched the wall, as the scene unfolded before him, palace aides rushing into the hallway to drag him from the window.

Bastardes! Shouted Antoine, This is not the eternal revolution! This is massacre! 

[b]The Bombing[/b]

Henri sat in shock as news flowed in that the Rosenmarkket regime had ordered the bombing of a group of protesters in Belgarde.

They did what?! Half shouted Eleonore.

Apparently according to some of our sources, the initial command was to bomb the Sallach forces, someone changed the command, replied the aide.

Do we know who?! Asked Henri.

We suspect Begren, your majesty,

Id assume it was to try and dissuade any secession movement, replied Henri.

Most likely, but the intelligence have received a communication that the temporary administration of Belgarde wants to talk, replied the aide

Oh, so now they want to talk, scoffed Henri, After bombing their own protestors,

And some pilot went along with this?! Asked Eleonore.

We do not know,

Henri placed his face into his hands and sighed frustratedly.

Wed be willing to engage in talks with the administration of Belgarde, but, I am not stopping Sallach from advancing, replied Eleonore.

Well they might not have an option to stop, the localised armies have been fleeing or have been surrendering, replied the aide.

Rosenmarkke shouldnt be collapsing this fast, however, replied Henri.

No, we never expected this, replied Eleonore.

[b]August 5, 2028: A Rapidly Escalating Situation[/b]

With the situation in Rosenmarkke and along the border undergoing radical shifts, concerns amongst the parties were raised regarding the push for unification, with most partymembers across the lines recognising that the secession of Knygta and Deyn was only the first of many.

It was thus, that on the evening of August 5 the heads of the various parties determined to meet at the home of Jean Luc Rousmonde for a discussion on what to do with the situation.

Thank you all for coming, stated Rousmonde, rising from his chair with a crystal glass in his hand, the other party heads nodded and raised their own glasses.

Now, as you know, the situation with which the king has dragged us into has led to a rapid collapse of the situation in Rosenmarkke, intoned Rousmonde, It is thus that I want us to consider the future, and where the hell this is all going,

Well, chairman, the general agreement amongst the members of my party, is that unification has become unavoidable at this point, I received word from a palace insider that Knygta and Deyn submitted their request to formally join Montfleur this morning, began Lilian Lucard.

The king will submit it to us no doubt, intoned Jacques Gusteau.

I doubt that, Jacque, it seems that the king has taken to his advisers and to the head of the government than to the party chambers, replied Rousmonde, Such a move shows that he may be preparing to sideline the parties in order to push through this unification process,

But unification is such a messy thing, interjected Rolande Perot, It would require vast referendums here in Montfleur, and place a massive burden on the state if not done well, I mean, look at the economy wed be inheriting, 

I do not disagree with that point, replied Gusteau, It is a risky move,

So we must take back the decision-making, replied Lucard.

Is there anything in the constitution? asked Gusteau.

We can issue a motion of censure, bar him from the chambers, replied Perot with a shrug.

The question is, would such a matter secure a vote majority? asked Rousemonde.

A good point, nodded Gusteau, As you may notice, compatriots, our right-wing friends are not here, and have made no effort to push back against the recent events, 

But they do not hold a majority, it should be no issue, replied Lucard.

They hold a slim majority, Lucard, two or three seats, replied Rousmonde.

Are there perhaps those who would oppose? The more moderate ones? asked Gusteau.

No, the moderates are too afraid of losing their seats in the next election, replied Perot.

The next election is soon is it not? asked Lucard.

It is in December, replied Rousmonde.

What are our polling positions looking like right now? asked Gusteau.

Well, unfortunately Li Baptistes are not doing so well in the polls, I would guess people are conflating us with the Strømmist ideology, began Rousmonde, The centrists, I believe they have  a lead no? he looked at Lucard and Gusteau.

Yes, the moderates are looking strong at this moment, but I do worry that might slide if this war begins to impact the economy, replied Lucard.

I doubt it will affect the economy, Rosenmarkke doesnt do or didnt do much major trade or business with us, beyond tourism, replied Gusteau.

So what are our options then, either we wrest the few right votes for a censure vote, or we wait for the elections? asked Perot.

We could petition the president, replied Gusteau, Request her to pass a war powers vote, 

Would a war powers vote work in stopping the king? asked Rousmonde.

It would potentially stall any motions to unite or accept any new regions without approval from the chamber, replied Lucard.

Then lets go with that, its mandated anyways, replied Gusteau.

I just worry about the votes, replied Rousmonde.

There is no need, it will be handled, replied Lucard, There are a few issues on the docket that the right need to have passed to secure a win in December.

Alright then, we shall do that, clapped Rousmonde, But if that fails, we will need to pivot to more drastic partywide motions, namely, strikes amongst the unions.

Strikes? asked Gusteau.

Yes, the king is not above the will of the people, and neither is the president, if the bourgeosie insist on acting like it is 1843 again, we shall treat them as such, replied Rousmonde sternly.

[spoiler=The Montfleur Crisis]

[b]The King Takes the Reigns[/b]

29 July, 2028

The King had been closely watching the situation regarding Montfleur and Rosenmarkke. He felt that he had to force his cabinet into taking act according to his will here, since he was the unifying political force in the country and the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces. 

He saw this as the perfect opportunity to exert the NABs official opinion on the conflict and inflict a blow to Rosenmarkke, a threat to Montfleur, a fellow member of the NAB. Not only that, but the NAB itself could not afford a member nation to lose a military conflict, so the King knew this very well. Not too long ago, they had just rejected a membership application from another country for not being developed enough in that regard.

The King pressed the ringer at the end of his desk, and his personal secretary walked in, bowing low.

Do-yun, summon the Prime Minister please.

Certainly, sir. he said, bowing before turning around and going to complete the task the King had told him to do.

Within an hour, the Prime Minister was getting out of his car, where the King was waiting for him.

Prime Minister.

Your Majesty. the Prime Minister said, bowing.

As you know, Ive summoned you here to talk about Montfleur and its situation with Rosenmarkke. Follow me to the Audience Room. Could we get something for you? Perhaps a fruit punch, a tea, coffee?

I could go for a coffee, yes. Thank you, Sir.

The King also let Do-yun know to summon the Heads of the Army before he walked into the Audience Room, to give him and the Prime Minister just enough time in the meeting to go over their plan to convince the Heads of the Army to agree with them before they arrived.

The King and the Prime Minister were now in the Audience Room, with the doors closed and the guards out of the room, though they were still outside the door for security purposes.

"Prime Minister, the situation in Rosenmarkke seems to be negatively impacting the government there Strømm government. The secession movement there is growing at a rapid pace and they want to join with Montfleur, as you know."

"Yes."

"Of course, I couldn't help but wonder about international speculation regarding Montfleur and its neutrality with this conflict, seeing that Rosenmarkke could use this as a pretense to start a military conflict with Montfleur, knowing that Montfleur is bound to respond."

"My deepest apologies, Your Majesty." Do-yun said, walking into the room, bowing. We've just received word that Rosenmarkke has declared war on Montfleur."

"Good Heavens." the King responded. "Alright, Do-yun. Thanks for letting us know."

Do-yun bowed and left the room.

"Sir, what do you suggest we do?"

"Well, the reason I called you here today is for you to assist me in convincing the Heads of the Army to agree with our stance that Montfleur is not violating the NAB's neutrality policy in this conflict, on top of the fact that we have just heard that Rosenmarkke declared war first, not Montfleur. You do agree with this, don't you?"

The Prime Minister realized that he was being pressured by the King to respond favorably. He didn't disagree with the King, in fact, he agreed with him, but for a few seconds briefly reflected on the King's words, seeing as the King rarely pressured his ministers into agreeing with him.

"Yes, I do. How would we convince them, Sir? I don't think we'll have a problem with them, but it is according to expectation that we inform them of the matter as well I assume?"

"Well, we'll do to them as I have just done to you, Prime Minister." the King said, smiling.

"I'm sorry Sir, I don't understand."

"I nudged you into supporting my take on this."

The Prime Minister's face turned red. He knew he wasn't supposed to answer right away that he knew what the King meant, but he knew from the start that he was referencing his tone of voice about the issue. Nonetheless, he returned the smile and laughed nervously.

"Oh." the Prime Minister said, forcing some more nervously laughing. "I can do that, Sir. I do that to the Opposition all the time on universally supported topics."

At this, the King laughed.

"I bet you do. I'm going to make it so that General Kwon of the Air Force already agrees with me, speaking to him in a more direct way about the situation, seeing as he is my strongest supporter among their group, you already know this. You're going to build on this and speak to them in a tone similar to mine, just speak in a casual way like they are already in agreement with us, but engage in conversation with me too to make it sound like you are also being told this in the same way I am telling them before you back me up."

The King pressed another ringer at the end of the table next to him.

"Certainly, Sir."

Do-yun walked in again, bowing.

"The Chiefs of Staff of the Army, Navy and his Commandant of the Marine Corps, and Air Force, Sir."

"Thank you, Do-yun. Send them in."

The King and Prime Minister stood up, and the Heads of the Army walked in, all bowing.

"Gentlemen, please sit down." said the King, gesturing to the seats in front of him.

"The Prime Minister and I just had our weekly briefing." 

Thankfully, the King had this excuse as to why the Prime Minister was in the Audience Room, since it was their briefing day anyways.

"As you know, Rosenmarkke has a major secession movement happening in the country, and as you have just heard, Rosenmarkke has declared war on Montfleur. Seeing as Montfleur is a fellow member of the NAB, I feel that we should make an official statement on behalf of the NAB that Montfleur is not violating its our neutrality policy, particularly in the military aspect, seeing as Rosenmarkke is the one who first declared war and is historic Montfleurois territory."

"General Kwon, I'll start with you first, since you are the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. What is your take on this?"

"Well,"

Again, the King's aide-de-camp walked into the room, bowing low.

"Your Majesty, Your Excellencies, we've just received word that the provinces of Knygta and Deyn have seceded from Rosenmarkke."

"Thank you, Do-yun." the King said, as Do-yun bowed and left the room.

"General, please continue."

"Yes, Sir. My take on this whole situation was magnified after hearing that Rosenmarkke declared war on Montfleur, and now even more so when I see that there is a chance for Rosenmarkke to fall. If there have been successful attempts to break away from Rosenmarkke, then we know that Montfleur has a chance at reunification as the dominant power between Rosenmarkke and itself. Rosenmarkke is Montfleur."

"Your Majesty, if I may say something regarding this?" the Prime Minister said, sounding like he was new to the conversation.

"Sure, go ahead."

"Generals, I feel that we can cooperate in this regard. We would like the announcement for our supporting of Montfleur in this conflict to come from the military, and then for us to back you up, seeing as we wouldn't want this to look like a political decision. We wouldn't want the opposition getting ideas..."

The Chief of Staff of the Army spoke up.

"Well, we wouldn't want to get involved in politics. We could say what we have to say militarily and then you could say what you have to say politically."

The King sensed a point of tension, not major, but enough to get his attention. So, he intervened to calm the situation.

"Leave that to me, General. The people need to hear from their King to confirm such a major decision, so I will address the nation and give the NAB's official stance on this issue after both of your press briefings. Why not say that the military stance of the NAB is that Montfleur is not the hostile military power and that it is acting purely in self-defense, in line with neutrality standards? As for you, Prime Minister, let's have you give the NAB's political stance: that the people of Rosenmarkke deserve to be free and that Rosenmarkke is rightful Montfleurois territory. Reiterate the message saying that Montfleur is acting purely in self-defense as well."

"I will make an official address to the nation stating Minhokae's thoughts on all of this and grant Montfleur permission to tap into the NAB's Equilibrium Development Bank, used in situations or circumstances where member nations of the NAB agree to send economic aid to other member nations in need, should they request it and their request be approved."

"Sir, when the military has its press conference, should we at the Navy also say something similar, or be in the audience to back General Kwon up?" asked the Chief of Staff of the Navy.

"Precisely my question." the Commandant of the Marine Corps said, relaxing in his chair and snapping his fingers at the Navy Chief of Staff. 

The King reached back and picked up a peanut which he threw to Commandant of the Marine Corps, as well as everyone else in the room.

"Everyone will give their usual press conference updates pertaining to their department. General Kwon will speak for the Armed Forces as a whole regarding the situation with Rosenmarkke and Montfleur." replied the King, calmly before standing up.

"Gentlemen, great to have you here today. Keep me in the loop." [/spoiler]
